claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd like to ask you a few more questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

(For example, is he attending school, college, sixth form, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure to be honest. I mean, he's 17, so I know he's past the age where school is mandatory, but I don't know the specifics of what counts as "approved" education or training. He might be doing something, but I couldn't tell you for certain what his situation is right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. Let me ask a different question that might help:

**Does Alex do any paid work? And if so, do you know roughly how many hours per week he works?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - or at least not that I'm aware of. He's not doing any paid work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Let me ask a couple more questions:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's not claiming anything like that himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now let me ask about your living situation:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. A few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care - meaning you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me and I provide for all his needs - his food, clothes, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just clarify one more important point:

**Going back to Alex's education or training situation - you mentioned you're not sure of the specifics. Can you tell me anything at all about what Alex does during the day? For example, does he attend any kind of school, college, sixth form, training program, or course? Or has he left education entirely?**

This is important because for 16 and 17 year olds, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really don't know, I'm afraid. I can't tell you whether he's in any kind of education or training at all, or what he does during the day in that regard. I just don't have that information.

## Assessment Summary

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**What we know:**
- You meet the basic requirements (you live in the UK, Alex lives with you, you're responsible for his care and provide for all his needs)
- Alex is 17 years old
- He's not working and not claiming any benefits himself
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**The key issue:**
For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're under 20 **and** staying in approved education or training. Since you don't have information about whether Alex is currently in any approved education or training, I cannot determine if you would be eligible.

**What you should do:**
To find out if you're eligible, you'll need to establish whether Alex is:
- Attending school, college, sixth form, or an approved training course
- Or if he has left education/training entirely

Once you have this information, you could contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly, or come back with those details and I can help you assess your eligibility.
